measurement_roots_note: Symbolic names a measurement block may run in. Blocks reference these by name and cannot name a path directly — that is what keeps a block from pointing a command at an arbitrary directory. `$REPO` means this repository, so those measurements run correctly on any checkout. `coreos` is a separate private repository and will not be present on your machine: those measurements report `unverifiable_here`, which is deliberately distinct from a failed check. Set EPISTACK_ROOT_COREOS=/path/to/doctrine-labs to run them if you have it.
note: The recursive case: this tool adjudicating claims about its own author. Lineage grouping is doing real work here — five measurement blocks resolve to two repository-state lineages, because a commit count and a test count read from one working tree at one commit are one observation of the world read two ways. The two deliberately flawed blocks resolve to a single subject-assertion lineage, because a rarity claim and the funnel supporting it were written by the same person and are not two pieces of evidence.

coreos-repo-state.label: Core OS repository, working tree at time of capture
coreos-repo-state.description: One system state. Commit count, test count, and first-commit date are three readings of it, not three independent observations. Independently re-runnable by anyone with the repo.

epistack-repo-state.label: FLF Epistemic Stack repository, working tree at time of capture
epistack-repo-state.description: A second system state, genuinely independent of Core OS: different repository, different history, separately checkable.

provider-timestamps.label: Third-party provider timestamps (Perplexity, git)
provider-timestamps.description: Clocks owned by parties other than the subject. The nineteen-day span is bracketed by two of them, which is why it is the strongest claim in the case and not merely the most flattering.

subject-assertion.label: The subject asserting things about himself
subject-assertion.description: Both deliberately flawed blocks resolve here. This is the lineage the case exists to expose: an assertion restated in a second form is still one assertion.

coreos-repo:git-log.title: Core OS commit count
coreos-repo:git-log.author: git
coreos-repo:git-log.independence_note: Re-runnable. Grouped with the other Core OS readings because they share one working tree.

coreos-repo:npm-test.title: Core OS test count
coreos-repo:npm-test.author: node --test
coreos-repo:npm-test.independence_note: Same working tree as the commit count. Counting these as two independent facts about productivity would be the exact error this tool detects.

coreos-repo:git-log-reverse.title: Core OS first-commit date
coreos-repo:git-log-reverse.author: git
coreos-repo:git-log-reverse.independence_note: Third reading of the same repository state.

epistack-repo:git-log.title: Epistemic Stack commit count
epistack-repo:git-log.author: git
epistack-repo:git-log.independence_note: A separate repository from Core OS, so a separate lineage.

epistack-repo:npm-test.title: Epistemic Stack test count
epistack-repo:npm-test.author: node --test
epistack-repo:npm-test.independence_note: Same working tree as the epistack commit count.

perplexity-export-2026-08-03.title: Provider-issued activity timestamps
perplexity-export-2026-08-03.author: Perplexity AI, git
perplexity-export-2026-08-03.independence_note: Two providers bracket the nineteen-day interval. Neither timestamp is revisable by the subject, which is what makes this tamper-evident rather than self-reported.

builder-self-assertion.title: The subject's claims about his own rarity
builder-self-assertion.author: Brandon Flores
builder-self-assertion.independence_note: Both flawed blocks resolve here on purpose. The rarity funnel and the correlation companion are one person's assertion stated twice — the same shape as one debate producing six documents in the COVID case.
